name: Cusco Quechua
variant: Quechua of Cusco (Cuzco-Collao), spelling of the Academia Mayor
region: Cusco, eastern Apurímac, northwestern Puno and the highlands of Arequipa, in Peru
summary: The Quechua of Cusco, the old Inca capital: runasimi, «the people's language». With its aspirated and ejective consonants, it is one of the most widely spoken varieties of the whole family.

conjugator.label: Verb
conjugator.hint: Type the verb as in the dictionary, ending in -y: rimay «speak», mikhuy «eat», riy «go», llank'ay «work». You can also type just the root (rima).

own.hint: Type any verb ending in -y and its meaning in English. The endings are the same for every verb.

source.short: Cusihuamán, Gramática quechua Cuzco-Collao (2001); AMLQ, Diccionario (2005)
source.full: Antonio Cusihuamán G., Gramática quechua Cuzco-Collao (Cusco: Centro Bartolomé de Las Casas, 2nd ed., 2001), for the verb; Academia Mayor de la Lengua Quechua, Diccionario quechua–español–quechua / Qheswa–español–qheswa simi taqe (Cusco, 2nd ed., 2005), for the spelling and the vocabulary; also a Quechua grammar handbook and a Quechua teaching manual. Spelling of the Academia Mayor, with five vowels.

about: Cusco Quechua, or Cuzco-Collao, is spoken in the department of Cusco, in eastern Apurímac, in northwestern Puno and in the highlands of Arequipa. With over a million speakers, it is one of the largest Quechua varieties, and the most written.

It belongs to Southern Quechua, together with the Quechua of Ayacucho, Bolivia and Argentina, which its speakers understand well. It stands out for its aspirated (ph, th, chh, kh, qh) and ejective (p', t', ch', k', q') consonants, taken from Aymara, and for q, said at the back of the throat.

It was the language of the Inca court in Cusco. Today it is official in Peru alongside Spanish, and it is kept alive by the Academia Mayor de la Lengua Quechua, bilingual schools, radio, music and a long tradition of poetry and theatre.

orthography.intro: We use the spelling of the Academia Mayor de la Lengua Quechua of Cusco, the one in its dictionary and in Cusihuamán's grammar. Each sound has its letter: q for the uvular sound, h after a consonant for aspiration and an apostrophe for the ejectives.
notes: q is said further back than k, at the back of the mouth: qocha «lake». At the end of a syllable it sounds like a strong Spanish j: soqta «six» sounds «sojta».

Aspirates are written with h and said with a strong puff of air: phaway «run», khuchi «pig». Ejectives are written with an apostrophe and said with a small catch: t'anta «bread», k'ayra «frog». They appear only once per root and never in suffixes.

Next to q the vowels i and u open up and are written e and o: qocha, erqe, orqo. That is why the Academia Mayor writes five vowels; the official alphabet of the Ministry of Education (1985) uses only three and writes qucha, irqi, urqu.
Stress falls on the second-to-last syllable and isn't written: rimani, rimarqanki. It is only marked on a few words stressed on the last syllable: arí «yes», alaláw «how cold!».
Loans from Spanish sometimes keep b, d, g and f: bindiy «sell», dusi «noon», kafiy «coffee».

grammar.intro: A Quechua verb is a root and a chain of suffixes: first those that change the meaning (-chi, -ku, -pu, -mu), then tense, person and last the enclitics (-mi, -si, -chu). The root is the infinitive without -y: rimay → rima-.

items.description: -chi make someone do, -ku for oneself, -naku each other, -pu for someone, -mu towards here…
-mi I saw it, -si I was told, -chá maybe, -chu ? / not.

blocks.title: The persons
blocks.description: There are two «we»: ñoqanchis includes the listener and ñoqayku doesn't. The future has endings of its own in the 1st and 3rd persons.

blocks.title: Two pasts
blocks.description: With -rqa- the speaker tells what they lived or saw. With -sqa- they tell what they were told, what happened in a dream or while drunk, or what they have just discovered.

cells: He went to Cusco (I saw it).
They say he went to Cusco.
This coffee turned out to be hot!

items.translation: I'm from the city of Cusco.

blocks.title: Suffixes that change the verb
blocks.description: They go between the root and the tense, and they can be combined.

blocks.title: Who to whom
blocks.description: The verb also marks who the action goes to: -wa- towards me, -su- from him to you, -yki from me to you.

tenses.name: Past
tenses.description: What happened and one saw or lived (-rqa-).

tenses.name: -sqa past
tenses.description: What happened without one seeing it: they say, it turns out (-sqa-).

tenses.name: Past habitual
tenses.description: What one used to do: -q and kay.

tenses.name: Conditional
tenses.description: What would happen or could be done (-man, -waq).

tenses.name: Imperative
tenses.description: Orders to you or you all (-y, -ychis).

tenses.name: Let's
tenses.description: Inviting others to do something together (-sunchis), often with haku.

lexicon.note: A weather verb, used mostly in the 3rd person: paran «it rains», parashan «it is raining».
